WARN 2012-06-19 12:45:00.588 [http-8080-2] (JAXRSUtils) No operation matching request path "/fedora/objects/test%3Aobject" is found, Relative Path: /test%3Aobject, HTTP Method: GET, ContentType:
;q=0.8,. Please enable FINE/TRACE log level for more details.
Thanks for the report. I noticed this while testing 3.6 as well. Sounds like a regression that needs fixing.
I'm going to hold out sanity testing gsearch until this is fixed, so I can run our islandora test suite against it.
I have produced a test that exhibits this behavior and have dug in a bit into why it's happening.

According to the spec, in JAX-RS, the value of the string given for a @PathParam is automatically URL-decoded. This can be prevented by specifying the @Encoded annotation for the argument. However, none of Fedora's REST code uses this annotation. So I wanted to find out: what would be causing CXF to fail to automatically decode these pid @PathParam values for us, when the spec says it should be?
Looking at the code, I noticed as part of the move to CXF, the @Path("{pid}") annotations where changed to specify a regular expression, like "{pid : ([A-Za-z0-9]|
Rolling this change back to use plain old "{pid}" fixes the issue. But I want to understand the purpose of the introduction of the pid regex first.
When testing the Fedora 3.6-preview against Islandora I noticed that Fedora doesn't seem to accept URL encoded PIDs anymore. Islandora URL encodes all the parameters sent to the Fedora REST API.

;q=0.8,. Please enable FINE/TRACE log level for more details.

,. Please enable FINE/TRACE log level for more details.
This looks like a new issue in 3.6, the above examples work fine against 3.5 and 3.4.2

renderedFields.description:
When testing the Fedora 3.6-preview against Islandora I noticed that Fedora doesn't seem to accept URL encoded PIDs anymore. Islandora URL encodes all the parameters sent to the Fedora REST API.

This works:
http://fedora36test:8080/fedora/objects/test:object
but this doesn't:
http://fedora36test:8080/fedora/objects/test:object

Logs:
WARN 2012-06-19 12:45:00.588 [http-8080-2] (JAXRSUtils) No operation matching request path "/fedora/objects/test%3Aobject" is found, Relative Path: /test%3Aobject, HTTP Method: GET, ContentType: /, Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,/;q=0.8,. Please enable FINE/TRACE log level for more details.

On ingest:
This works:
curl -u fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin -X POST http://fedora36test:8080/fedora/objects/test:object
But this doesn't:
curl -u fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin -X POST http://fedora36test:8080/fedora/objects/test%3Aobject

Logs:
WARN 2012-06-19 11:28:47.975 [http-8080-1] (JAXRSUtils) No operation matching request path "/fedora/objects/test%3Aobject" is found, Relative Path: /test%3Aobject, HTTP Method: POST, ContentType: /, Accept: /,. Please enable FINE/TRACE log level for more details.

This looks like a new issue in 3.6, the above examples work fine against 3.5 and 3.4.2
